chapter_theme: The gross five letters (தூல பஞ்சாக்கரம்): the fifty letters that make all the Vedas and Agamas resolve into the five letters of Nandi's name, which are placed in the body and recited aloud. Said with the mouth and held in the heart, they make nectar well up, show the way of grace past rebirth, and protect the soul at death; those who ignore them whirl like splashing water.
structure_note: The letters and their reduction to five (2698 to 2700); the five set in the body (2701); their power at death and in rebirth (2702, 2705 to 2707); reciting them aloud (2703, 2704); and those who do not know their greatness (2708).

2698.reading: The fifty letters are all the Vedas, the fifty letters are all the Agamas, and once one knows the order of the fifty letters, the fifty letters are the five letters.
2698.nuance: ஐம்பது எழுத்து is the full alphabet of mantra theory (fifty or fifty-one letters). அடைவு (order, arrangement) suggests the letters set out in a diagram, as in the earlier chakra chapters. The claim is that all scripture reduces to the five letters.

2699.reading: Beginning with A it becomes fifty-one, rising from U, ending in M and dying away again and again as it climbs; Nandi's name begins with Na.
2699.nuance: A, U and M are the parts of Om, and the verse seems to trace speech from A through Om to its dying away, then to the five letters beginning with ந (நமசிவாய). மாய்ந்துமாய்ந்து ஏறி may describe the sound fading as it rises in the body.

2700.reading: Para joined with the sixteen from A; Isan, the inner light, with his Shakti from U; Siva from Si, the Veda and the triangle; and from Na the root mantra is reached.
2700.nuance: ஈரெண் (the sixteen) are taken as the sixteen vowels from அ. கோணம் (angle, triangle) may be a diagram in which the letters are set. மூலமந்திரம் (root mantra) is taken as the five letters beginning with ந. The correspondences are technical and I can't fix them.

2701.reading: Mouth, throat, heart and navel, then the linga, above them that opening, a pure segment, and going to the crown of the head: these are the places, five with five, of the five letters.
2701.nuance: The verse maps the five letters onto places in the body, some of them the adharas. இலிங்கம் here is taken as the genital centre. அவ்வாய் and தூயதோர் துண்டம் are obscure, and ஈறாம் ஐந்தோடு ஆம் may mean the five places with five more, or the five letters at the five ends.

2702.reading: When the seven rays blaze up and the soul rises leaving its instruments, and when Death lays hand on it to change its life, it is the five letters that bring protection.
2702.nuance: The seven rays (கிரணங்கள் ஏழும்) are unclear: perhaps the seven bodily elements burning up at death, or seven inner lights. கரணங்கள் are the instruments of the soul (mind and the rest). அரணம் is the fortress or shelter the mantra gives.

2703.reading: At the time when sun and moon rise and are spoken of, no one knows the fitting mantra; but one can recite with the mouth and praise the holy five letters of the red-eyed one.
2703.nuance: Sun and moon are traditionally the right and left breaths, so the first line may refer to the moments of breath rather than the sky. சேயுறு கண்ணி (she of red or distant eyes) may be Shakti, whose letters these are. The verse sets plain recitation against hidden lore.

2704.reading: Say 'Sivaya nama' once, so that clear nectar wells up and nectar wells in the heart; those who do not wish to drink that welling flood of nectar whirl about like splashing water.
2704.nuance: சிவாய நம is one of the orders of the five letters. The welling nectar can be read devotionally as the sweetness of the name or yogically as the amrita that flows from the head. The whirling of those who refuse is commonly taken as the round of births.

2705.reading: For those who, standing in the qualities that are the guru's way, can cut the reckoning that is the womb's way and refuse so that the coming way dies, it is the five letters that show the way of grace.
2705.nuance: The verse plays on வழி (way) four times: the guru's way, the womb's way, the way of coming (into birth) and the way of grace. கணக்கு (the reckoning) is the account of karma that leads to rebirth.

2706.reading: When the soul comes, stunned by the frenzy of karma, recite Nandi's holy letters, which press close; if you dwell on what they point to, they join you to his ringing anklets, and one who knows that pointing takes the form of the king of austerity.
2706.nuance: வெறிக்க வினைத்து is obscure: perhaps the soul dazed by karma, or coming into birth by karma. குறிப்பு (what is pointed to) is the meaning behind the letters. தவம் கோன் உரு may mean Siva's form or the form of a great ascetic.

2707.reading: Thinking in the heart, saying 'Lord' with one's mouth, and at the time of sleep saying 'your paired feet are my refuge', one can win the grace of the Lord of the five, who dwells on the northern mountain where clouds crawl.
2707.nuance: துஞ்சும் பொழுது may be the time of sleep or of death; in this chapter, after 2702, death is likely. அஞ்சில் இறைவன் may be the Lord in the five letters or the Lord of the five elements. The northern mountain is Kailasa.

2708.reading: Not grasping the greatness of the five the Lord set down, will poor people go on with their empty talk? The wide earth, above and below and in every way, is wholly encircled by the serpent.
2708.nuance: இராமாற்றம் is obscure: it may be 'talk of the night' or 'unsteady words'. The last two lines may mean that the earth is bound by the serpent (Adisesha), or by the serpent of bondage; how they answer the first two is unclear.

links.note: 965, in the chapter on the chakra of the holy hall, is nearly the same verse; there the fifty letters 'go' and become the five (எழுத்தும்போய்), here they simply are the five. The repetition ties the five letters of this chapter to the earlier letter diagrams.

Both begin from the letter A as the first of all letters. The Kural uses it as a simile for the Lord as first of the world; Tirumular traces the letters from A through Om to Na, the first letter of Nandi's name, so the alphabet itself leads to the Lord.
2094 tells people to worship the Lord daily until they sleep (துஞ்சும் அளவும்); 2707 gives the words for that hour, calling him Lord and his feet refuge.

2704 says that saying Sivaya nama makes nectar well up; 2709, opening the next chapter, makes the same formula an alchemical pill that turns the body to gold. Both give the recited name a bodily effect.

2701 sets the five letters in places of the devotee's body, mouth, throat, heart, navel and on to the crown (இருமத்தகம்), five with five. Thiruppugazh 1165 makes the Lord's own form of the five letters: na the two feet, ma the belly, si the chest, va the mouth, and ya the crown (நகரமிரு பாதமாகி மகரவயிறாகி). The same mapping of na-ma-si-va-ya onto a body is made once on the reciter and once on the god, which is the meeting point the recitation aims at.

2702 says that when the soul rises leaving its instruments and Death lays hand on it (மரணம்கை வைத்து), it is the five letters that bring protection (அரணம்கை கூட்டுவது அஞ்செழுத்தாமே). Thiruppugazh 75 draws Yama in full and asks Murugan to come on his peacock at the hour of his coming, to a servant who has the refuge (தஞ்சமாகிய) received from generation to generation. Both name a single guard at the moment of death; for the Tirumanthiram it is the mantra itself, for the Thiruppugazh the god's coming in person.

2703 says that no one knows the fitting mantra (ஆயுறு மந்திரம் ஆரும் அறிகிலார்), but one can recite the holy five letters with the mouth (வாயுற ஓதி). 962 says those who recite the six letters do not know them (ஓதும் அறிவார் அறிகிலர்), and that life is won only by those who can utter it as one letter with no other. 962 adds a condition that 2703 leaves out: recitation counts when it is gathered into one, not merely spoken.

2705 says that for those who cut the reckoning of the womb's way (கருவழியாய கணக்கை அறுக்க), it is the five letters that show the way of grace. Thiruppugazh 525 asks that, chanting 'Saravanabhava ... guru' and melting in Tamil, his birth and death end (சனனம் மரணமதை ஒழிவுற) and he reach Sivam. Both make a mantra the means of ending rebirth; the Tirumanthiram's is the five letters with the guru's way, the Thiruppugazh's the six letters of Murugan's name.

2708 asks whether poor people, not grasping the greatness of the five the Lord set down (பிரான்வைத்த ஐந்தின் பெருமை உணராது), will go on with empty talk. 980 says what follows once the truth of the five letters is known (அஞ்செழுத்து உண்மை அறிந்தபின்): the Supreme stays firm in the heart and there is no ruin to the house. 980 supplies the gain that 2708's people miss by not knowing.

source_issues: 2698 nearly repeats 965; the last line differs (965: ஐம்பது எழுத்தும்போய் அஞ்செழுத் தாமே), which slightly changes the sense from becoming to being.
2701 lines 2 and 3 (அவ்வாய், தூயதோர் துண்டம்) and 2708 line 2 (இராமாற்றம்) are obscure and may be corrupt.
